title: Volvo Says Driverless Trucks Are Coming to Texas in 2027
key_facts: Volvo previewed its VNX heavy-duty vocational trucks at its Shippensburg, Pennsylvania, plant on 23 Sep; production starts in mid-2027.
Nils Jaeger, president of Volvo Autonomous Solutions, told Autoweek Volvo will be on Texas roads without safety drivers in the first quarter of 2027.
He said Volvo expects 300 trucks hauling freight hub to hub in Texas by the end of 2027.
Routes named are Dallas to Houston, Fort Worth to El Paso and Dallas to Oklahoma City; Arizona follows in the second half of 2027.
The driverless trucks use the Aurora Driver from autonomous trucking company Aurora.
Volvo says its autonomous business could reach $3 billion in five years; partners providing loads include DHL, DSV and Uber Freight.
quote_evidence: Nils Jaeger, president of Volvo Autonomous Solutions, told Autoweek, “We will be on the Texas roads in Q1 of 2027 without safety drivers.
By the end of 2027, we will have 300 trucks transporting freight hub-to-hub, and then scale from there.
Volvo has also said industrial scaling will begin in 2028, and that its autonomous business could reach $3 billion in five years.
why_it_matters_hint: Driverless long-haul trucking in Texas is being scheduled for early 2027, but these are company plans.
event_date: Volvo VNX preview 23 Sep 2026; interview dates not stated
notes: Plans and targets, not a deployment yet.
